Aggregate Health Data into Time Series

Source: R/sus_data_aggregate.R
sus_data_aggregate.Rd

Aggregates individual-level health data into time series counts by specified time units and grouping variables. This function is essential for preparing data for time series analysis, DLNM models, and other temporal epidemiological methods.

Usage

sus_data_aggregate(
  df,
  time_unit = "day",
  fun = "count",
  group_by = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  complete_dates = FALSE,
  date_col = NULL,
  backend = "arrow",
  lang = "pt",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df (stage "stand" or later, typically from sus_data_standardize(), sus_data_create_variables() or the sus_data_filter_*() functions), or an Arrow/DuckDB lazy table.

time_unit

Character scalar, default "day". Temporal unit:

  • Standard: "day", "week", "month", "quarter", "year".

  • Multi-period: "N days" / "N months" (e.g. "5 days" pentads, "14 days", "3 months", "6 months"). "2 weeks" is not supported; use "14 days".

  • Special: "season" (Brazilian seasons DJF, MAM, JJA, SON). Anything else aborts with "Invalid time_unit".

fun

Character scalar, or a named list/vector, default "count". Valid values: "count", "sum", "mean", "median", "min", "max", "sd", "q25", "q75", "q95", "q99". A named list, e.g. list(mean_temp = "mean", max_temp = "max"), computes several statistics of value_col. Anything other than "count" requires value_col. Invalid values abort.

group_by

Character vector of column names to group by, e.g. c("sex", "age_group"). NULL (default) = no extra grouping. The municipality column of the system (residence/occurrence/establishment code, detected automatically) is always kept as a grouping key when present. Missing columns abort.

value_col

Character scalar, column to aggregate when fun is not "count" (e.g. "temperature", "pm25"). Ignored for "count".

complete_dates

Logical scalar, default FALSE. If TRUE, fills missing periods (per group) so the series has no gaps; filled values are 0 for fun = "count" and NA otherwise.

date_col

Character scalar, name of the date column. NULL (default) auto-detects it by system (e.g. admission date for SIH, death date for SIM, notification date for SINAN); aborts if none is found.

backend

Character scalar, "arrow" (default) or "tibble". "arrow" aggregates lazily (Arrow/DuckDB) and collects only the small result; it falls back to "tibble" with a warning if it fails. "tibble" processes in memory.

lang

Character scalar, "pt" (default), "en" or "es". Language of messages and of the smart column names.

verbose

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Print progress messages.

Value

A climasus_df tibble (sus_meta: stage = "aggregate", system preserved, temporal = start/end/unit) with:

  • date: start of each period (Date)

  • the municipality column and any group_by columns

  • aggregated column(s): for fun = "count" a name derived from the system and lang (e.g. n_deaths/n_obitos, n_hospitalizations/ n_internacoes, n_cases/n_casos); otherwise one column per fun (list names are used when fun is a named list)

Details

Pipeline position: after sus_data_create_variables() / filtering; before the spatial join, climate linkage and modelling steps.

Features:

  • Multiple aggregation functions: counting, or sum/mean/median/ percentiles of value_col.

  • Smart column naming: the count column is named from the health system (e.g., n_deaths for SIM, n_hospitalizations for SIH-RD, n_births for SINASC, n_cases for SINAN, n_procedures for SIA, and n_establishments for CNES).

Epidemiological Use Cases:

  • Daily/Weekly: Standard time series analysis, DLNM for short-term effects

  • Pentads (5 days): Heat wave analysis, smoothing daily noise

  • Fortnightly (14 days): Diseases with longer incubation periods

  • Monthly: Seasonal patterns, long-term trends

  • Quarterly: SUS management reports, policy evaluation

  • Seasonal: Dengue, Influenza, respiratory diseases aligned with Brazilian climate

  • Yearly: Long-term trend analysis, climate change impacts

Brazilian Seasons (when time_unit = "season"):

  • Summer (Verao): December-January-February (DJF)

  • Autumn (Outono): March-April-May (MAM)

  • Winter (Inverno): June-July-August (JJA)

  • Spring (Primavera): September-October-November (SON)

See also

sus_data_create_variables(), sus_data_filter_cid(), sus_data_plot_aggregate_ts(), sus_data_plot_aggregate_map()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(climasus4r)

# Basic daily aggregation
df_daily <- sus_data_import(uf = "SP", year = 2023, system = "SIM-DO") %>%
  sus_data_standardize() %>%
  sus_data_filter_cid(disease_group = "respiratory") %>%
  sus_data_aggregate(time_unit = "day")

# Pentad aggregation (5-day periods) for heat wave analysis
df_pentad <- sus_data_aggregate(df, time_unit = "5 days")

# Fortnightly aggregation for diseases with longer incubation
df_fortnightly <- sus_data_aggregate(df, time_unit = "14 days")

# Monthly aggregation by municipality
df_monthly <- sus_data_aggregate(
  df,
  time_unit = "month",
  group_by = c("race", "sex"),
  lang = "pt"
)

# Quarterly aggregation for SUS reports
df_quarterly <- sus_data_aggregate(df, time_unit = "quarter")

# Seasonal aggregation for dengue analysis (Brazilian seasons)
df_seasonal <- sus_data_aggregate(
  df,
  time_unit = "season"
)

# Weekly aggregation by age group and sex
df_weekly <- sus_data_aggregate(
  df,
  time_unit = "week",
  group_by = c("age_group", "sex") #age_group comes from `sus_data_create_variables()`
)
} # }
